title: Integral realization of a specified normalized system adjunction
statement: For D,l,E,X,Y,f,c as in integral reconstruction, fix rX:Reconstruction l E X, rY:Reconstruction l E Y, s:Systems l E c and a:SystemAdjunction l E c s [def-sf-exceptional-integral-reconstruction-interfaces]. There exists a compatible replacement transport record t on the same ordinary adjoint, sites, proper/open word and comparison such that the conjugated integral adjunction has a Realization l E c D hl rX rY (s with transport := t) (a.withTransport l E c s t): normalized systemLeft comparison, uniform bounds, additive exact functors with coherent adjoint shifts, prescribed compact-support finite-Tor lift, the primitive ambient realization and its actual integral normalization equation, with all displayed comparison shifts. The normalized adjunction fields are copied by withTransport to the updated Systems parameter; its functors and transpose equation do not depend on transport shifts. The transport is chosen compatibly, rather than assuming arbitrary triangulated shift fields have the cochain normalization.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29, 3.16; Section 5, especially Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; blueprint exceptional inverse-image construction. Integral reconstruction steps in the existing exceptional coefficient construction.

proof.text: Choose the localized cochain shifts of the actual proper/open word and of its transported right adjoint, rebuilding the transport record t on the same ordinary adjoint and site/proper-open comparisons. Take canonical system operations and their ordinary-limit model. The scalar-unit and proper/open site squares give the supportProjection normalization of systemLeft, and finite bounds give the two UniformBounds assertions. An arbitrary previous transport shift is not identified with this chosen normalized shift. Exact open extension retains the input cohomological and Tor intervals at the intermediate open object, so the single proper/open word satisfies its finite-Tor realization domain.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29, 3.16; Section 5, especially Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; blueprint exceptional inverse-image construction. Integral reconstruction steps in the existing exceptional coefficient construction.

proof.text: Conjugate the system adjunction by rX and rY. K-flat reduction and K-injective total limit are additive and exact. Use the actual sequence-site and reduction/limit shift equations to paste coherent integer shifts. The adjoint shift is unique, so the right shift equals rightAdjointCommShift; triangulated adjunction gives right exactness.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29, 3.16; Section 5, especially Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; blueprint exceptional inverse-image construction. Integral reconstruction steps in the existing exceptional coefficient construction.

proof.text: The whole-system direct comparison for the single proper/open word identifies the reduction tower with the prescribed compact-support tower. Its open-adjunction mate and the inverse open completion unit, followed by the projection-normalized proper direct-image/limit comparison, give realization and primitive in the stated order. Direct and recursive comparisons agree. Faithful full inclusion lifts realization followed by inverse prescribedRealization to identification, proving normalization on actual integral maps.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29, 3.16; Section 5, especially Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; blueprint exceptional inverse-image construction. Integral reconstruction steps in the existing exceptional coefficient construction.

proof.text: Termwise quotient, exact open, proper derived and signed Roos-cone shift squares paste on this word. They give the two composite shifts, realization and prescribed realization shifts; lift the latter shift and use faithful inclusion for identificationShift. The cochain sign identities ensure addition, zero and negative-shift coherence.

lean.statement:
theorem exceptionalIntegralRealizationAssembly
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f)
    (rX : Reconstruction l E X) (rY : Reconstruction l E Y)
    (s : Systems l E c) (a : SystemAdjunction l E c s) :
    ∃ t : ExceptionalSystemTransport s.right s.siteX s.siteY s.siteZ
      s.properOpen s.comparison,
      Nonempty (Realization l E c D hl rX rY { s with transport := t }
        (a.withTransport l E c s t))
